Riemann, in English

A reader for Levent Alpöge's Lean archive (with Claude), announced 2026-11-20 · mirror commit 7cbf7a0 · built 2026-11-22

What this is. A walk down the Lean proof from the five headline theorems, with each step put into plain English. The Lean is the source; the English is a reading of it.
Status of the proof. Claimed, not yet independently reviewed. This reader did not build the code or run #print axioms. A text scan of all 175,187 files (by the mirror) found no sorry, axiom or native_decide.
How the walk was made. Every declaration was indexed as text (no Lean elaborator), names were resolved by namespace rules, and the graph was walked breadth-first from Main.lean. 1,057,672 declarations indexed; 755,915 are reachable from the main theorems; 856 of the heaviest are shown here, 146 of them translated by hand.

The statement

-- Mathlib, NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean
def RiemannHypothesis : Prop :=
  ∀ (s : ℂ) (_ : riemannZeta s = 0)
    (_ : ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1)) (_ : s ≠ 1),
    s.re = 1 / 2

-- this archive, src/Main.lean
theorem riemannHypothesis : RiemannHypothesis := rhOfAll

Take any complex number s where the Riemann zeta function is zero.

Set aside the "trivial" zeros at −2, −4, −6, …, and the point s = 1 (where ζ has a pole, which Mathlib assigns a junk value).

Then the real part of s is exactly ½.

The headline statement is Mathlib's own definition, written by the Mathlib community and not by this archive. That matters: a proof can only be as faithful as the statement it proves.
